claims.text: Structural stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles at high temperature is governed by optimization of nanoparticle composition and structure.
Integrating experimental synthesis and characterization with simulations enables the composition and structure governing stability to be optimized.
The as-synthesized nanoparticles vary in composition and structure.
Nanoparticle composition and structure will be varied using experimental synthesis and simulation methods.
An optimized nanoparticle composition and structure enhances thermal stability and resistance to degradation.
Enhanced thermal stability and degradation resistance allow nanoparticles to maintain performance during high-temperature service.
Optimized nanoparticles will exhibit a 20% increase in stability relative to unoptimized nanoparticles under the same temperature and application conditions.
Stability can be assessed through retention of nanoparticle structure and composition.
The proposed hypothesis applies to catalytic service at 773–1173 K and thermoelectric service at 473–1923 K.
The catalytic test regime is intended to use nanoparticles with low noble-metal content.
Failure of optimized nanoparticles to achieve at least 15% higher stability than unoptimized nanoparticles would falsify the hypothesis.
